case_name: B. Virupakshaiah and another v State of Karnataka and others
facts: an FIR was lodged on 22.11.2005, at Toranagallu Police Station by Sheikh Hussain Sab (PW3), stating that he and his colleague Basavana Gouda (PW2) were working as Security Guards in Aqua Minerals Factory

when they were on duty on 22.11.2005, at about 1:30 PM, while taking food they heard a bang sound from outside and immediately they went out and saw that a Bolero Jeep had dashed against Tata Indica Car on N.H.
They saw four unknown persons pulled out two inmates of Indica Car and assaulted on their head, face and hand with sharp edged weapons, causing heavy bleeding injuries
One of the deceased named Bhimaneni Kondaiah died on the spot whereas the other deceased Pavadappa died on way to the hospital
issues: whether the prosecution has established the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt
whether the High Court was correct in acquitting the accused
petitioner_arguments: the testimonies of the eye-witnesses, wherein PW1, PW4, PW5 and PW6 have specifically stated the number of persons present as well as the individual act committed by each of the accused/ respondents in the incident
the recovery of the weapon used and the Indica Car involved in the incident cannot be overlooked
respondent_arguments: material alterations between the testimonies of the eye-witnesses were pointed out to prove that PW1, PW4, PW5 and PW6 were not material eye-witnesses
the conduct of the eye-witnesses was argued to be unnatural and their silence in not making any statement to the police officers at the earliest, casts doubt in their testimonies
court_reasoning: the prosecution case revolves around the testimonies of the eye-witnesses, the existence of conspiracy and the recovery of the alleged weapons
there are material alterations in their statements from the testimonies of PW2 and PW3, and even with the deposition of PW71 i.e. the Investigating Officer
cases_cited: B. Virupakshaiah and another v State of Karnataka
